appearance_facts.fact: The May bar is a very short dark-red rectangle whose top is only slightly above the x-axis, far below the 10,000 gridline.
Five other bars (Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar) are tall dark-red rectangles ranging from about 17,500 to 40,000 on the y-axis.
All bars share the same dark-red fill; the May bar is visually the smallest by a large margin.

printed_facts.fact: Axis label 'Month' with categories in order: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May.
Approximate values: Apr ≈ 29,500; Jan ≈ 40,000; Jun ≈ 17,500; Feb ≈ 20,000; Mar ≈ 27,000; May ≈ 800 (well under 10,000).

public_definitions: Routing criterion field: 'May low-pumping severity route'.
Option: 'Route May to standard low-pumping follow-up'.
Option: 'Escalate May to critical low-pumping anomaly review'.
Option: 'Send May to background monthly record filing'.
uncertain: No explicit numeric threshold on the chart distinguishes 'standard follow-up' from 'critical anomaly'; the May value is read as approximately 800 m3, clearly the lowest bar.
No data labels are printed on the bars, so the May value is estimated from its position relative to the 10,000 tick.
